finding.claim: Host allowlist uses endswith("example.com") without a leading dot, so attacker-owned domains such as attackerexample.com pass the check, and the server then fetches them with httpx (including any IP they resolve to, e.g. 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1).

trace.note: url: str taken directly from the query string
endswith("example.com") without dot boundary; ALLOWED_SUFFIX=".example.com" (line 7) is defined but unused
c.get(url) fetches the unmodified attacker URL; response length returned at line 17

finding.guards_checked: Userinfo tricks (http://169.254.169.254@example.com/) connect to example.com -> safe. Fragment/query @ tricks rejected by hostname check -> safe. Non-http schemes rejected by httpx -> safe. Redirects: relied on httpx default follow_redirects=False (unverified against pinned version). No resolved-IP / private-range check, no port restriction. Backslash parser differential between urlparse and httpx not verified (UNCERTAIN, not reported). /ping (mirror.py:20-24) uses constant URL -> unreachable sink.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, which is a suffix match without a dot boundary and does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is defined but never used. There is no exact hostname set check, no resolved-IP or private-range check, and no port restriction.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) is unauthenticated input (route at mirror.py:10 has no auth dependency), and mirror.py:13 accepts any hostname ending in "example.com", such as attackerexample.com, which mirror.py:16 then fetches unmodified with httpx. All trace lines match the code, and the impact is limited to the response length returned at mirror.py:17.
